profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a public company, traded as NVDA, founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California. Its most recent 10-K, covering a period ending 2026-01-25, reported revenue of $215,938,000,000. The company's own site presents it as a builder of enterprise agentic AI, centered on the Nemotron family of multimodal foundation models.

According to the site, Nemotron is a family of multimodal, open models built for long-running, self-evolving agents, which the company describes as delivering high reasoning throughput and leading accuracy for complex agent workflows, including graduate-level science, advanced math, visual understanding, retrieval-augmented generation, speech, and safety. The site names Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for specialized tasks and NeMo Switchyard for routing each step to the right model. Nemotron models are offered as NVIDIA NIM microservices, which the company says require an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license, and are also released under the NVIDIA Open Model License, described as permissive and permitting commercial deployment without crediting NVIDIA. The site lists supporting tools including NVIDIA NeMo, NVIDIA Blueprints, NVIDIA Dynamo, TensorRT-LLM, SGLang, and vLLM, and hardware including NVIDIA RTX PRO and NVIDIA DGX Spark. Bryan Catanzaro, VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, is quoted on the vision behind Nemotron, and ServiceNow is cited among ecosystem partners.

Two NVIDIA products are tracked here: NVIDIA Nemotron, in the chat and general LLM category, noted for synthetic data generation, GPU optimization, and self-hosted options, and NVIDIA NIM, in the cloud AI services and model APIs category, noted for inference microservices, enterprise GPU optimization, and self-hosted options. The company's litigation exposure record lists 281 cases in California.
